question.problem:
The volumes of some chocolate muffins before cooking are normally distributed with a mean of $57\,\text{ml}$ and a standard deviation of $2\,\text{ml}.$
In contrast, the volumes of some pumpkin muffins before cooking are normally distributed with a mean of $42\,\text{ml}$ and a standard deviation of $1\,\text{ml},$ while the volumes of some blueberry muffins before cooking are normally distributed with a mean of $48\,\text{ml}$ and a standard deviation of $1.5\,\text{ml}.$
During cooking, it is known that chocolate muffins double in volume, while pumpkin and blueberry muffins triple in volume.

If a chocolate muffin, a  pumpkin muffin, and a blueberry muffin are randomly selected after cooking, what is the probability that the sum of their volumes is less than $400\,\text{ml}?$ You may assume that the volumes of the muffins are independent. 

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9842\,$ | $\,0.9846\,$ | $\,0.9850\,$ | $\,0.9854\,$ | $\,0.9857\,$ |
| $\,2.2\,$ | $\,0.9878\,$ | $\,0.9881\,$ | $\,0.9884\,$ | $\,0.9887\,$ | $\,0.9890\,$ |
| $\,2.3\,$ | $\,0.9906\,$ | $\,0.9909\,$ | $\,0.9911\,$ | $\,0.9913\,$ | $\,0.9916\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let ${X}_{1}$, ${X}_{2},$ and ${X}_{3}$ denote the volume of the chocolate, the pumpkin, and the blueberry muffins, respectively. Then, we have

$$
{X}_{1}∼N(57,{2}^{2}),\,{X}_{2}∼N(42,{1}^{2}),\,{X}_{3}∼N(48,{1.5}^{2}).
$$

Let the random variable $Y$ denote the total volume of the randomly selected chocolate, pumpkin, and blueberry muffins after cooking. Since the chocolate muffin doubled in volume, while the pumpkin and blueberry muffins tripled in volume during cooking, we have

$$
Y=2{X}_{1}+3{X}_{2}+3{X}_{3}.
$$

The random variable $Y$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =(2\cdot 57+3\cdot 42+3\cdot 48) \\  & =384 \\ \text{Var}[Y] & ={2}^{2}\cdot {2}^{2}+{3}^{2}\cdot {1}^{2}+{3}^{2}\cdot {1.5}^{2} \\  & =4\cdot 4+9\cdot 1+9\cdot 2.25 \\  & =45.25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
Y∼N(384,45.25).
$$

In order to find $P(Y<400),$ we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y<400) & =P(Z<\frac{400-384}{\sqrt{45.25}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<2.38) \\  & =Φ(2.38)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(2.38)≈0.9913.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>0) & ≈Φ(2.38) \\  & ≈0.9913.\end{aligned}
$$
